headline: Recommended $1 million for Kennedy Schoolyard and $500,000 for Union Square Plaza; kept Block 9 tax agreement in committee.
summary: Recommended a $48,000 recycling grant, a $350,000 Magoun Square grant, and a $12,075 salary adjustment for six employees. Funds from the Community Preservation Act for historic buildings, a Veterans Cemetery, and a Spring Street green space were recommended. A police road safety grant of $60,313.17 was kept in committee while police respond to questions about cyclist enforcement.

## City of Somerville, Massachusetts City Council Finance Committee Meeting Minutes

Thursday, November 19, 2026

6:00 PM

This meeting was held via Zoom and was called to order by Chair Wheeler at 6:00 pm and adjourned at 9:22 pm on a roll call vote of 4 in favor (Councilors Link, Strezo, Scott, and Wheeler), 0 opposed, and 1 absent (Councilor Hardt).

Also present: Lisa Robinson - Director of Community Wellness, Michael Richards- Infrastructure Director of Finance, Alexander Cherry - Recycling and Waste Manager, Alan Inacio - Strategy and Development Director of Finance and Administration, Brad Rawson - Director of Mobility, Kimberly Wells - Chief Administrative Officer, Anne Gill - Director of People Operations, Emily Wisdom - Somerville Police Department Finance and Administration Director, Michael Holland - Somerville Police Lieutenant, Roberta Camerson - Preservation Act Manager, Catherine Lester Salchert - Special Counsel, Tom Galligani - Executive Director of Strategy and Development, Katherine Wiese - Economic Development Planner, Barry Abramson - President of Abramson and Associates and Consultant to the City, Ellen Shachter - Director of Housing Stability, Lisa Davidson - Director of Housing and Delaney Fisher-Cassiol - Clerk of Committees

Roll Call

- Present: City Councilor At Large Jon Link, City Councilor At Large
- Kristen Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas
- (J.T.) Scott and City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler

Absent:

Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt

1. Committee

Approval of the Minutes of the Finance Committee Meeting of October 28, Minutes

2026.

(ID # 26-1664 )

- RESULT: ACCEPTED
- AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Health and Human Services

2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $50,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1601 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Department of Agriculture to the Health and Human Services Department-Community Wellness Division for

- the Somerville Mobile Farmers Market.

This item was discussed with item #26-1602.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $50,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1602 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Department of Agriculture to the Health and Human Services Department-Community Wellness Division for

- the continued operation of school-based food access programs.

- Lisa Robinson, Director of Community Wellness, explained that the first

grant will increase the City’s ability to purchase fresh, locally grown produce for the mobile farmers market and allow the program to continue

next year. The other grant will support the continuation of the school markets and Care Card program. Councilor Link expressed his support.

Chair Wheeler asked whether the funding would be sufficient to meet the programs’ needs. Director Robinson noted that additional funding could be

requested but that the current award puts the mobile market in a good position to continue. She also clarified that the school market funding is

- supplemented through the General Fund.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Infrastructure

4. Mayor's Request Requesting approval for a time-only contract extension for Water & Sewer

(ID # 26-1582 ) printing and mailing services with D3 Logic Inc.

- Michael Richards, Director of Finance, noted that the contract expires on

June 30 and that sufficient funds are available to support the extension. The contract ceiling is being increased to account for the additional months, which have already been budgeted for the year. Rather than establishing two

separate contracts within one year, the City plans to extend the existing contract. In response to a question from Chair Wheeler, Director Richards

explained that the contract is $55,000 annually and will be increased by 25% to account for the extension and potentially additional mailers. He noted that

they anticipate exhausting all available funds. Councilor Link asked for clarification, noting that he understood the request for additional time to mean that no additional funding was involved. Director Richards clarified

that contracts extending beyond three years require City Council approval, so the request is for approval of the additional time and the additional

- expenditure does not require approval.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Department of Public works

5. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $48,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1619 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Department of Environmental

- Protection to the Department of Public Works for recycling and waste
- reduction efforts, including food waste containers.

- Alexander Cherry, Recycling and Waste Manager, explained that the grant is
- awarded through MassDEP’s Recycling Dividends Program under the

Sustainable Materials Recovery Program. Somerville has received this funding based on its recycling activities since 2015. The grant has two

components: $36,000 for approved small-scale expenditures, such as recycling and trash totes or household hazardous waste events, and $12,000

for food waste drop-off equipment, including compost bins. Councilor Link asked how the compost drop-off program has been going. Manager Cherry

reported that the program has collected more than 2,000 pounds of food waste in its first three weeks. He added that seven of the bins have been so

popular that they require twice weekly pickups, while the remaining three are serviced once a week.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Mobility

6. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $500,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1596 ) match required, from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban

Development to the Strategy and Development Mobility Division for the Union Square Plaza Phase 1 Project.

- Brad Rawson, Director of Mobility, explained that this is a request to accept

earmarked federal funding secured through the City’s congressional delegation. He noted that the City developed a multi-phase strategy several

- years ago to improve streetscapes and public spaces throughout Union

Square, with the Prospect Street and Webster Avenue intersection identified as the first priority. The project is currently at the 25% design stage, and the City is pursuing opportunities for external funding to support the estimated

- $15 million project. Councilors Link and Scott expressed their support, with

Councilor Link noting the project’s importance for people traveling throughout the City. In response to a question from Chair Wheeler, Director

Rawson explained that the City has coordinated the project with other planned improvements in the area to ensure the construction work is

complementary. Councilor Link asked whether the project would create a more cohesive design along Webster Avenue and coordinate with

MassDOT’s bridge project. Director Rawson confirmed that the City has coordinated with MassDOT and incorporated its design plans. As part of the project, Big and Little Newton Streets will be realigned to intersect more

effectively with Webster Avenue, shortening pedestrian crossing distances and improving bicycle safety.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

7. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $350,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1612 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Executive Office of Economic

- Development (EOED) to the Strategy and Development Mobility Division
- for the Massachusetts Downtown Initiative Capital Grant Improvement .

- Brad Rawson, Director of Mobility, explained that the project focuses on
- Broadway in Magoun Square and is part of the City’s Safe Streets initiative.

- The City anticipates putting the project out to bid this winter, with

construction beginning in the summer. The improvements are intended to enhance safety and mobility throughout the area. Councilor Strezo noted that

several businesses in Magoun Square have expressed concern about the potential impact of construction on their operations. Director Rawson

- explained that the project is currently at the 80% design stage and that the

City is in the midst of a month long public engagement period. He noted that the City is continuing to engage with nearby businesses through three rounds

of business outreach and has made design modifications based on their feedback. Councilor Strezo also raised concerns about people riding scooters

- on sidewalks and delivery drivers stopping in unsafe locations. Chair

Wheeler echoed these concerns and emphasized the importance of ensuring accessibility throughout the area. Councilor Link noted that when he lived in

the area, he was consistently able to find parking, although intersections in the area often became congested.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Administration

8. Mayor's Request Requesting to use available funds in various departmental Salaries accounts

(ID # 26-1607 ) totaling $12,075 to adjust Fiscal Year 2027 salaries for positions with

- updated job duties as a result of the Fiscal Year 2027 departmental
- reorganization.

- Kimberly Wells, Chief Administrative Officer, explained that several
- positions were eliminated or consolidated during the current fiscal year.

- Following these changes, some employees assumed additional

responsibilities beyond what was originally anticipated, prompting requests for a review of their compensation. She noted that City positions are

assigned grades based on their responsibilities and that several positions required regrading to reflect the additional duties and responsibilities.

- Councilor Scott clarified that the request involves raises or promotions for

six employees. Chair Wheeler highlighted the transparency of the grading review process.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Police Department

9. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to use available funds in the Police Salaries and Other

(ID # 26-1606 ) Lump Sum Payments accounts in the amount of $25,950 to correct the grading of the Victim Witness Advocate and Senior Crime Analyst positions

- to align with the compensation study.

- Anne Gill, Director of People Operations, explained that the compensation

study, which began in 2023, identified grading discrepancies in two civilian positions that had not been graded correctly. She clarified that these

positions were included in the original compensation study and that the requested corrections are unrelated to the reorganization that took place

during the current fiscal year. Kimberly Wells, Chief Administrative Officer, confirmed this and noted that the positions themselves will not change. She

added that she does not anticipate any further changes resulting from the compensation study.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

10. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $60,313.17 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1581 ) match required, from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts Executive Office

of Public Safety and Security to the Somerville Police Department for the Municipal Road Safety Grant Program.

- Emily Wisdom, Somerville Police Department Finance and Administration

Director, explained that the City receives this grant annually and uses the funding to supplement the Traffic Unit’s ability to perform traffic safety

duties outside of its regularly scheduled hours. The grant supports targeted traffic safety campaigns focused on motor vehicles and cyclists, as well as

pedestrian and cyclist safety outreach and education. Councilor Link noted that the Council is still awaiting additional information in response to a

previous order. Director Wisdom clarified that while the grant specifies certain time periods for the campaigns, a slight delay in implementation

could be accommodated. Councilor Link expressed that he was not comfortable supporting the grant until the requested information was

provided. Councilor Scott noted a pattern in previous years in which the grant was primarily used to harass cyclists and expressed hope that the grant

- would again be rejected, as it was in 2022.

Chair Wheeler asked for clarification on the enforcement component of the grant. Michael Holland, Somerville Police Lieutenant, reported that only six

warning citations had been issued to cyclists under the grant during the past year. He emphasized that the department's focus is not on bicycle violations

but on promoting safety. Director Wisdom added that the intent of enforcement is educational and that the data does not indicate a high volume

- of citations issued to cyclists.

- Councilor Link described an incident in Union Square in which a female

cyclist proceeded through an intersection during a pedestrian crossing signal and was repeatedly stopped by police, leaving her visibly upset and crying.

He clarified that his concern was not necessarily the issuance of citations but whether certain behaviors were being discouraged or encouraged, noting that

using pedestrian crossing signals can sometimes be the safest way for cyclists to navigate certain intersections. He also recalled that City staff had recommended this approach when Washington Street was redesigned.

- Councilor Strezo emphasized that any interactions with cyclists should be

educational rather than harassing. She added that some cyclists disregard traffic signals and endanger pedestrians, particularly seniors and expressed

support for the grant, noting that it has been received for many years and cautioning against making blanket statements about its use.

- Chair Wheeler shared an example of a cyclist proceeding through a red light

at School Street and Somerville Avenue when there were no pedestrians or vehicles present. He noted that the cyclist shared with him that he was an

immigrant from Israel and expressed concern that being stopped by police had him fear for his status in the country, even if the interaction resulted

only in a warning. He noted a gap between the language of the grant and how enforcement is carried out by the department and expressed interest in

understanding how the funds would be used in practice. In particular, he referenced the discussion of Idaho stops as permissive on page 15 of the

attachment FFY2027 MRS Application - Somerville Police Department .

- Lieutenant Holland clarified that Idaho stops remain illegal in Massachusetts

but are not a priority for enforcement by the department. He offered to provide responses to any additional questions before the next meeting.

RESULT: KEPT IN COMMITTEE

20. Mayor's Request Requesting that $15,154.25 from the Fiscal Year 2025 Community

(ID # 26-1589 ) Preservation Act grant to the Elizabeth Peabody House for Siding

Replacement be repurposed for structural reinforcement.

Alan Inacio, Director of Finance and Administration for Strategy and Development, introduced the items related to this year’s funding application

round. He explained that the Elizabeth Peabody House requests are related to rising construction costs. The organization has applied for CPA funding

- for several years and initially requested $230,000 for exterior work.

However, previous grants and construction work revealed additional needs, prompting the organization to redirect previously awarded funding toward

- those expenses. Regarding the Veterans Cemetery in Clarendon Hill,

Director Inacio noted that significant restoration work was completed during last year’s grant cycle. During repairs to a historic fence, the contractor

discovered lead paint that had not been previously identified. This resulted in additional costs because the fence had to be removed and repaired off-site

- before being returned. Mission Church, a privately owned property on

Highland Avenue, was also included. Director Inacio explained that the City tries to avoid requiring applicants to return for multiple years of funding so

they encourage historical property applicants to complete a condition assessment upfront so that all necessary work can be included in one

- request.

- The Kennedy School is another multi-year applicant and required additional

funding this year because the original project budget was a preliminary estimate. The customized nature of the playground equipment for the all

needs park also resulted in additional costs. Director Inacio noted that park projects often include improvements to subsurface stormwater management

and runoff systems, which can require additional funding. In this case, an old underground structure was discovered that needed to be removed before the stormwater storage tank could be installed. Director Inacio also introduced

the Spring Street traffic item, which is a community-led project to create a pocket park between Summer Street and Somerville Avenue. The project

- will include traffic improvements and green space in the triangular area.

- Regarding the Armory, he explained that CPA funds can only be used for

historic preservation needs and that an exterior needs assessment will be conducted to determine which improvements are eligible for funding.

- Councilor Link asked about the Kennedy School project and why
- landscaping costs had decreased in the revised budget while other expenses

had increased in the attachment Finance - 2026-11-19 Kennedy Schoolyard

Comparison Budget (with 26-1592). Director Inacio agreed to follow up.

- Councilor Link also asked how community members could pursue similar
- neighborhood green space projects. Roberta Cameron, Preservation Act
- Manager, explained that residents interested in advocating for projects on

City-owned property can contact her by email or submit an intake form through the CPA webpage. The project would then be paired with a City

department to serve as its sponsor. Councilor Strezo asked whether the triangle green space project was the first of its kind in the City. Manager

Cameron confirmed that it was the first time a pocket park had been created from a traffic island, although neighborhood groups had collaborated on

similar projects in the past. Chair Wheeler also expressed interest in receiving a breakdown of the Kennedy School playground features.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

Strategy and Planning

21. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of the First Amendment to Easement and License

(ID # 26-1608 ) Agreement - 74 Middlesex Avenue.

- Catherine Lester Salchert, Special Counsel, explained that this amendment

modifies an existing easement to incorporate the landscape management plan. She noted that the easement includes hardscape areas used for

emergency access and that the original agreement consists of both an easement and a license. In response to a question from Chair Wheeler, Special Counsel Salchert clarified that no funding is required.

RESULT: RECOMMENDED TO BE APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Link, City Councilor At Large
- Strezo, Ward Two City Councilor Scott and City Councilor
- At Large Wheeler
- ABSENT: Ward Seven City Councilor Hardt

22. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of an Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing

(ID # 26-1611 ) (UCH-TIF) Agreement for Block 9 - Assembly Square.

- Tom Galligani, Executive Director of Strategy and Development, explained

that the City’s affordable housing consultants determined that medium and large scale housing projects are infeasible in much of Somerville, so the City

could miss opportunities to secure additional inclusionary housing units. He noted that the City evaluated three potential tools to address this issue:

changes to the inclusionary housing ordinance, upzoning and tax incentives.

- Given previous Council concerns about changing the inclusionary housing

ordinance and the long term nature of upzoning, the City is now exploring tax incentives.
